name: Kwakiutl

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Kwak'wala (kwak1269).

notes: Research. Northern Wakashan language of northern Vancouver Island and the adjacent British Columbia coast, written in the community (U'mista-style) practical orthography. Lateral obstruents (tł=[tɬ], dł, ł=[ɬ]), affricates ts/dz/ch, labialized kw/gw/xw and uvular q are mapped. Kwakʼwala has an extensive ejective/glottalized series marked by a raised apostrophe that this base map does not fuse, and schwa is not recovered from spelling, giving a substantial PER floor. Grapheme table checked against Boas (1947): no discrepancy found. STRESS EXEMPTION: Boas (1947) and later work (Bach 1975; Elfner 2024) describe Kwakʼwala prominence as quantity-sensitive (heavy syllables -- non-schwa vowels closed by a sonorant coda, or bimoraic vowels -- attract stress) and, in current analyses, assigned at the phrase level rather than as a fixed word-position rule; this is not a function this project's positional `stress` schema can express without a syllable-weight primitive keyed to the mora, so no `stress` block is added rather than encoding a wrong approximation.
